## Walkthrough

UCX shared and dedicated threads receive workers during construction and run as `std::jthread` instances. Their `run()` methods accept stop tokens. Stop callbacks wake shared-thread polling or stop the dedicated thread’s Asio context.

### Changes

**UCX thread lifecycle**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|---|---|
|**Thread startup and stop-token interface** <br> `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.h`, `src/api/cpp/backend/backend_engine.h`|`nixlUcxThread` receives its workers at construction and starts a `std::jthread` that passes its stop token to `run`. The promise-based startup and join methods are removed.|
|**Shared-worker polling and shutdown** <br> `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp`|The shared thread receives workers during construction and creates poll descriptors for them. It owns control-pipe descriptors with `nixl::scopedFd`; a stop callback writes to the pipe to wake `poll`, and the loop exits when the token is stopped.|
|**Dedicated-worker startup and shutdown** <br> `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_pool_engine.cpp`|Each dedicated thread receives its worker during construction and starts as a `std::jthread`. Its stop callback stops the Asio context. The request loop remains unchanged.|

**Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `433411d0`

**TL;DR:** Both failing stages on the aarch64 agents trace to `git clone https://github.com/...` failing inside the containers ("could not read Username for 'https://github.com'"), which kills `meson setup` on the required `taskflow` wrap-git subproject and silently drops the optional `prometheus-cpp` subproject, making 15 `prometheusTelemetryTest` cases fail. Fix by making these subprojects fetchable without git (tarball `wrap-file` like liburing, or pre-install them in the CI image) / restoring git egress on those agents.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** In build #3145, one aarch64 `Build` stage (node 437) failed at `meson setup`, and another aarch64 variant's `Test CPP` stage (node 493) failed with 15 `prometheusTelemetryTest` failures; both stem from GitHub git clones failing on the agent.

**Root cause:**
- Node 437 log: after HTTPS tarball fetches worked (`Downloading liburing source from https://github.com/...` succeeded), the git-based wrap failed:
  `Cloning into 'taskflow'... fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` / `fatal: expected flush after ref listing`, ending in
  `meson.build:233:16: ERROR: Git command failed: ['/usr/bin/git', ... 'clone', '--depth', '1', '--branch', 'v3.10.0', 'https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git', 'taskflow']`.
  `meson.build:233` declares `dependency('taskflow', fallback: ['taskflow','taskflow_dep'])` with no `required: false`, and `subprojects/taskflow.wrap` is a `[wrap-git]` — so a failed clone is a hard configure error. Plain HTTPS downloads work on the agent; the git transport/credential path does not (git prompts for a username, i.e. the request was rejected/intercepted rather than a DNS/network outage).
- Node 493 (Test CPP) failures are the same root problem in its optional form: every failure is `Plugin file does not exist: .../libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so` → `Failed to load prometheus telemetry plugin`. The matching `Build` log (node 415) install list contains `libtelemetry_exporter_doca.so` but **no** `libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so`, i.e. the plugin was never built. `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build:36` does `cmake.subproject('prometheus-cpp', required: false)` and only warns when it isn't found, and `subprojects/prometheus-cpp.wrap` is also `[wrap-git]` (`https://github.com/jupp0r/prometheus-cpp.git`, `clone-recursive = true`) — so the same clone failure degrades silently at configure time and surfaces as 15 test failures later. The gtest cases hard-`ASSERT` on the plugin handle instead of skipping.
- Nothing in the PR branch (`iyastreb/tp-3-threadpool-queue`) is implicated: the other four variants built and passed identical test sets, including `ucx_threadpool*` cases.

**Implicated commit:** Not a code regression. The fragile mechanisms were introduced by `76275cfc` "Use tagged Taskflow git wrap for NIXL builds (#2121)" (bzsuni) and `b8ca6d80` / `903629aa` (prometheus-cpp wrap, alexanderbilk / ovidiusm); the trigger is agent-side git egress to github.com.

**File:** `meson.build:233`, `subprojects/taskflow.wrap:1-4`, `subprojects/prometheus-cpp.wrap:1-5`, `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build:36-59`, failing assertions at `test/gtest/telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp:157` (and 233/288/352/387/430/544/561) and `test/gtest/telemetry_histogram_test.cpp:112,153`

**Suggested fix:**
1. Immediate: re-run on agents with working GitHub git access, or fix the aarch64 container/agent so `git clone https://github.com/...` works (proxy env passed to git, or `git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf` pointing at the internal mirror). Setting `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` will at least turn the hang-prone credential prompt into a clear error.
2. Durable: convert both wraps from `[wrap-git]` to tarball `[wrap-file]` with `source_url` + `source_hash` (as `liburing` already does — that download succeeded on the same agent), e.g. `https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow/archive/refs/tags/v3.10.0.tar.gz` and the prometheus-cpp v1.3.0 tarball; or pre-install taskflow/prometheus-cpp into the CI images so the fallback path is never taken under `PRE_INSTALLED_ENV`.
3. Make the failure honest instead of misleading: have the prometheus gtest fixture `GTEST_SKIP()` when `libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so` is absent, and/or make the prometheus subproject `required: true` when telemetry tests are enabled, so a missing dependency fails at configure time rather than as 15 opaque test failures.

**Related:** none

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` · commit `433411d0`

**TL;DR:** The vLLM Elastic EP test failed because the DL node ran out of disk space while downloading the DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat weights (`No space left on device`), not because of anything in PR #2280 — free/prune the HF cache and pyxis image cache on `gb-nvl-118-compute04` and pre-seed the model into a persistent cache.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage "Run DL NIXL EP tests" (node 176) failed: both `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[enforce_eager_heavy]` and `[cuda_graphs_heavy]` failed during model fetch, and `srun` returned exit code 1.

**Root cause:** Environmental disk exhaustion on the test node, not a code defect. All NIXL-side tests passed first (`no_expansion.json` and `expansion_fault_contraction.json` both completed, `==== nixl_ep elastic tests done ====`, RDMA variants skipped because `mlx5_1` is `PORT_DOWN` — an expected, handled skip). The failure occurs only in the vLLM stage, while `huggingface_hub` writes model shards:

```
E huggingface_hub.errors.HfHubHTTPError: Server error '500 ' for url '.../deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat/resolve/.../model-00003-of-000004.safetensors'
E No space left on device
```

The `500` from the Artifactory HF remote is wrapped around an underlying `ENOSPC` — the shard could not be written to the HF cache (`HF_HOME` is unset in the env dump, so it defaults to `/home/svc-nixl/.cache/huggingface`), and the download is retried/reported as a server error. Both parametrisations fail identically on the same shard, which is the signature of a full filesystem rather than a flaky mirror. Contributing pressure: this build's own pyxis image import into the node's local store took 13 minutes (07:42:15 → 07:55:37) for the aarch64 test image `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep-test:1268`, and each build imports a fresh image under a per-build container name (`nixl-ci-ep-1268`).

Build #1267 of the same job on the same pipeline passed all stages, confirming this is node state, not a regression from commit 433411d0 (`iyastreb/tp-3-threadpool-queue`, PR #2280) — that branch touches the NIXL threadpool/queue path, which is exercised by the elastic tests that succeeded.

**Implicated commit:** none — not a code regression. (Test harness last touched by c984ce65, lishapira, "CI: add vLLM + NIXL EP test to the EP CI job (#2154)", which introduced the unguarded model download.)

**File:** `.gitlab/test_ep.sh:136` (the `pytest tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py` invocation; env set at the srun call in the Jenkins slurm step)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Immediate: reclaim space on `gb-nvl-118-compute04` (slurm job 2277607) — prune `/home/svc-nixl/.cache/huggingface` and stale pyxis container images/squashfs from previous builds (`nixl-ci-ep-<older-build>`), then re-run #1268.
2. Prevent recurrence in `.gitlab/test_ep.sh`: before the vLLM block, export an explicit `HF_HOME` on a sized, persistent filesystem and pre-seed / reuse the DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat snapshot instead of re-downloading per build; add `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` once seeded so a cache miss fails fast with a clear message.
3. Add a cheap guard so this diagnoses itself: `df -h "$HF_HOME" /tmp /home/svc-nixl` in the `==== Show system info ====` section, and a pre-flight check that aborts with an explicit "insufficient disk for model cache" message if free space is below the model size (~30 GB) — this avoids the misleading `500` from the Artifactory proxy masking `ENOSPC`.
4. Have the CI job delete its pyxis container/image after the run so per-build images don't accumulate on the shared node.

**Related:** PR #2154 (added the vLLM EP test that downloads the model); PR #2280 / commit 433411d0 is the triggering change but is not implicated. No existing issue found for this ENOSPC signature — worth filing one against the DL EP CI job.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `433411d0`

**TL;DR:** The nixlbench container's "custom UCX" stage failed because UCX's GPUNetIO submodule could not be cloned inside the build (`fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'`), yet `configure` still enabled the MLX5 `gda` module, so `make` died on the missing `gpunetio/common/doca_gpunetio_verbs_def.h`. Fix by disabling the gdaki/GPUNetIO module in that build (or pre-populating the submodule in the CI-side UCX clone) instead of letting `autogen.sh` warn-and-continue.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage "Build image" (id 229, the nixlbench image with `UCX=custom`, arm64) failed at the UCX source build step with `make[5]: *** No rule to make target 'gpunetio/common/doca_gpunetio_verbs_def.h', needed by 'all-am'. Stop.`

**Root cause:** CI's "Prepare environment" clones UCX (`v1.23.x`) into `ucx-src` without `--recurse-submodules` (stage 172 log: `Cloning into 'ucx-src'... Switched to a new branch 'v1.23.x'`), and that tree is copied into the image via `COPY --from=ucx . /workspace/ucx`. Inside the build, `./autogen.sh` tries to fetch the submodule itself and fails twice:
```
Cloning into '/workspace/ucx/external/gpunetio'...
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
Failed to clone 'external/gpunetio' a second time, aborting
WARNING: Failed to update GPUNetIO submodule, continuing...
```
The warning is non-fatal, so the build proceeds; because the DOCA GPUNetIO/verbs dev packages *are* installed in `os_setup_stage`, `configure` enables the gdaki module (`configure: MLX5 modules: < gda >`), and `src/uct/ib/mlx5/gdaki` then needs the header that only exists in the un-fetched submodule → `make` error, `Error: building at STEP "RUN echo "INFO: Starting custom UCX build..."...: exit status 2`. No hang and no timeout: the whole stage ran 454 s with continuous output. This is a build-infrastructure defect, unrelated to PR #2280's thread-pool changes — a rerun will fail the same way.

**Implicated commit:** unknown for the failure trigger (not from `433411d0`); the UCX ref that introduced the gdaki/GPUNetIO submodule dependency was pinned in `226e76d7` — Mikhail Brinskiy, "build: bump UCX version to v1.23.x (#2163)"

**File:** `benchmark/nixlbench/contrib/Dockerfile:143-162` (configure invocation at lines 154-158); build context wiring at `benchmark/nixlbench/contrib/build.sh:129-137`

**Suggested fix:** Make the custom-UCX stage self-consistent instead of relying on a submodule it cannot fetch:
1. Explicitly disable the module in the nixlbench custom UCX configure, e.g. add `--without-gdaki` (UCX v1.23.x DOCA GPUNetIO option) next to `--without-gdrcopy --without-go` at `benchmark/nixlbench/contrib/Dockerfile:157`; or guard it: `if [ ! -f external/gpunetio/common/doca_gpunetio_verbs_def.h ]; then GDAKI=--without-gdaki; fi`.
2. If the `gda` transport is actually wanted, fetch it on the CI host where credentials exist — clone `ucx-src` with `--recurse-submodules` in the Jenkins "Prepare environment" step so the sources arrive via the `ucx` build context — and make `autogen.sh`'s submodule failure fatal in CI rather than a warning, so the real cause is reported at the clone instead of 90 s later in `make`.

**Related:** #2250 ("build: bump DOCA to 3.5") touches the same DOCA/GPUNetIO area; #2163 pinned UCX to v1.23.x. No existing issue tracks this submodule/gdaki build break.

</details>

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `Clang Format Check` · commit `882af2e4`

**TL;DR:** The Clang Format Check failed because two hunks in `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp` added by commit 882af2e4 don't match the repo's `.clang-format` (misaligned constructor parameters and a 101-char line); run `clang-format-19` on the file and amend.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** GitHub Actions job `clang-format` (workflow `.github/workflows/clang-format.yml`) exited 1 because `clang-format-diff-19` produced a non-empty diff for `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp`.

**Root cause:** Pure style violation, not a functional failure. `clang-format-19` with the repo's `.clang-format` (`AlignAfterOpenBracket: Align`, `ColumnLimit: 100`) reports two problems in the newly added code:
- Lines 39–40: the continuation parameters of the `nixlUcxSharedThread` constructor are indented 23 spaces instead of 24, so they don't align under the open paren of `nixlUcxSharedThread(` on line 38.
- Line 140: `thread_ = std::make_unique<nixlUcxSharedThread>(this, std::move(workers), init_params.pthrDelay);` is 101 characters, exceeding `ColumnLimit: 100`; clang-format wants the assignment broken after `thread_ =`.

The workflow checks only the diff of the last commit (`git diff -U0 HEAD^1 HEAD`), and both hunks were introduced by the head commit, so they were flagged.

**Implicated commit:** [REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String] — Ilia Yastrebov, "Moved jthread to derived classes"

**File:** `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp:38-40` and `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp:140`

**Suggested fix:** Apply the formatter's own output and amend the commit:

```bash
clang-format-19 -i -style=file src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp
```

Equivalent manual edits:
```cpp
    nixlUcxSharedThread(const nixlUcxEngine *engine,
                        std::vector<nixlUcxWorker *> workers,
                        nixlTime::us_t delay)
```
and
```cpp
    thread_ =
        std::make_unique<nixlUcxSharedThread>(this, std::move(workers), init_params.pthrDelay);
```
Note the check inspects only `HEAD^1..HEAD`, so the fix must land in the same commit that introduced the lines (amend/squash) rather than as a follow-up commit that reformats unrelated context — though a separate commit touching the same lines will also pass. Installing the repo's pre-commit clang-format hook locally would catch this before pushing.

**Related:** PR #2280 (this change); precursor PRs #2229 and #2221 touch the same file.

</details>

**TL;DR:** The `clang-format` check failed because two hunks added in commit 882af2e4 to `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp` don't match the repo's `.clang-format` — misaligned continuation parameters and a 101-character line over the 100-column limit. Run `clang-format-19 -i` on the file (or apply the two-line diff from the log) and push.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** The `clang-format` job in the Clang Format Check workflow exited 1 because `clang-format-diff-19` produced a non-empty reformat diff for `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp`.

**Root cause:** Genuine style violations in the newly added code — not an infra or tooling problem. The job installs `clang-format-19` successfully, enumerates four modified C/C++ files, and reports two required reformats:

1. `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp:38-40` — the `nixlUcxSharedThread` constructor's continuation parameters are indented 23 spaces, but `.clang-format` sets `AlignAfterOpenBracket: Align`, which requires 24 spaces (aligned with the column after `nixlUcxSharedThread(`). clang-format wants to add one space to both `std::vector<nixlUcxWorker *> workers,` and `nixlTime::us_t delay)`.
2. `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp:140` — `thread_ = std::make_unique<nixlUcxSharedThread>(this, std::move(workers), init_params.pthrDelay);` is 101 characters, exceeding `ColumnLimit: 100` (`.clang-format:40`), so clang-format wants to break after `thread_ =`.

Both lines were introduced/touched by the PR's head commit. Note the workflow's step runs under `bash -e` and pipes the diff to `clang-format-diff-19`, so any non-empty suggestion output makes the step fail — the check is working as designed.

**Implicated commit:** 882af2e4 — "Moved jthread to derived classes", Ilia Yastrebov (2026-09-23T13:38:34Z); the same PR's earlier commit 433411d0 ("Use jthread") touched the same region.

**File:** `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp:38-40` and `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp:140`

**Suggested fix:** Apply the formatter's own output locally and amend/push:

```sh
clang-format-19 -i --style=file src/plugins/ucx/ucx_thread_engine.cpp
```

Or make the two edits by hand:

```cpp
    nixlUcxSharedThread(const nixlUcxEngine *engine,
                        std::vector<nixlUcxWorker *> workers,
                        nixlTime::us_t delay)
        : nixlUcxThread(engine, std::move(workers)) {
```

```cpp
    thread_ =
        std::make_unique<nixlUcxSharedThread>(this, std::move(workers), init_params.pthrDelay);
```

To avoid this class of failure recurring on this branch, consider enabling a `pre-commit` hook with the `clang-format` mirror pinned to version 19 so the same formatting is enforced before push.

**Related:** PR #2280 (this change); the file was previously restructured by #2229 and #2221.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `99dd5d66`

**TL;DR:** The aarch64 `Build` stage failed because meson's `wrap-git` fetch of the `taskflow` subproject aborted — `git clone https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git` got an auth challenge and died with "could not read Username for 'https://github.com'" — nothing to do with the PR's code; convert `subprojects/taskflow.wrap` to a `wrap-file` tarball (as liburing/tomlplusplus already are) or pre-vendor taskflow in the CI images.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage 386 ("Build", aarch64 variant) failed after 6 s during `meson setup nixl_build`: `ERROR: Subproject taskflow is buildable: NO / Git command failed: git clone --depth 1 --branch v3.10.0 https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git`.

**Root cause:** Dependency-fetch failure, not a code defect. On the aarch64 agent the anonymous `git clone` of taskflow was answered with a credential prompt and failed instantly:
```
Cloning into 'taskflow'...
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
fatal: expected flush after ref listing
...
meson.build:233:16: ERROR: Git command failed: ['/usr/bin/git', ... 'clone', '--depth','1','--branch','v3.10.0','https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git','taskflow']
```
Plain HTTPS egress on that same agent was fine — the `liburing` and `tomlplusplus` wrap-file tarballs downloaded from github.com seconds earlier. Only the git-transport path failed (no credential helper / no tty, GitHub or the egress proxy returning a 401 to the anonymous fetch). The x86_64 variants of the same build (e.g. stage 480) cloned taskflow successfully in ~12 s and the same aarch64 stage passed in build #3151, so this is an intermittent/environment-dependent fetch, and `taskflow` is the only dependency still fetched via `[wrap-git]`, which is why it is the one that breaks. The PR under test (#2280, jthread/stop_token) is unrelated — the failure happens before any compilation.

**Implicated commit:** 76275cfc — bzsuni, "Use tagged Taskflow git wrap for NIXL builds (#2121)" (introduced the `[wrap-git]` taskflow dependency); triggering commit 99dd5d66 is innocent.

**File:** subprojects/taskflow.wrap:1-5 (consumed at meson.build:233)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Preferred: replace the git wrap with a hashed tarball wrap so it uses meson's HTTP download path, which also supports a fallback mirror and doesn't need git credentials:
```ini
[wrap-file]
directory = taskflow-3.10.0
source_url = https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow/archive/refs/tags/v3.10.0.tar.gz
source_filename = taskflow-3.10.0.tar.gz
source_hash = <sha256 of the tarball>
patch_directory = taskflow

[provide]
taskflow = taskflow_dep
```
2. Complementary hardening: pre-populate `subprojects/packagecache` (or vendor taskflow) in the CI docker images so no build-time network fetch is needed, and/or set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` plus a retry around subproject fetches so the failure mode is a fast, clearly-labelled retry rather than a silent credential prompt.
3. Re-run build #3152 — the current failure will very likely not reproduce.

**Related:** PR #2121 (introduced the taskflow git wrap); PR #1577 (precedent: "Use liburing wrap" via wrap-file). Failing build: nixl-ci-non-gpu #3152, stage 386.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `99dd5d66`

**TL;DR:** The container build failed in `contrib/Dockerfile` at the gRPC step — `git clone --recurse-submodules` of grpc/grpc couldn't fetch nested submodules from github.com ("could not read Username… No such device or address"), an anonymous-fetch/rate-limit failure on GitHub, not a code defect in the PR. Retry the build and/or make the gRPC clone resilient (retry loop, non-interactive git credential config, drop unneeded nested submodules).

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** All four parallel "Build image" branches of `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` #759 aborted at Dockerfile STEP `RUN git clone --recurse-submodules -b ${GRPC_TAG} ... grpc/grpc` with `exit status 128`.

**Root cause:** Transient GitHub fetch failures while recursing submodules of grpc v1.73.0. Two distinct branches show the same signature at different nested paths:
- arm64 branch (stage 211, 13:53:10): `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` / `fatal: expected flush after ref listing` → `Unable to fetch in submodule path 'third_party/bloaty/third_party/protobuf/third_party/googletest'; trying to directly fetch 5ec7f0c4…` → `Direct fetching of that commit failed` → `Failed to recurse into submodule path 'third_party/bloaty'`.
- stage 233 (14:01:02): same error on `third_party/protobuf`, commit `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]`.

That error string is git falling back to interactive credential prompting after GitHub returned a non-200 (typically anonymous-clone rate limiting/throttling) for an unauthenticated HTTPS fetch. Evidence it is environmental, not the PR: the very same nested submodule (`bloaty/.../googletest` @ `5ec7f0c4…`) that failed at 13:53 succeeded at 13:59 in stage 233; the build clones ~40 repos from github.com in a tight loop, and there are no large timestamp gaps (each failure is immediate). The PR under test (`iyastreb/tp-3-threadpool-queue`, commit 99dd5d6) touches no build or container files, and the failure occurs long before any NIXL source is compiled.

**Implicated commit:** unknown — not caused by a repo commit; the gRPC clone step itself is long-standing (`contrib/Dockerfile` last touched by d2495941, NirWolfer, unrelated to this step).

**File:** contrib/Dockerfile:178

**Suggested fix:**
1. Immediate: re-run build #759 — the failure is retryable and already self-healed once mid-build.
2. Durable hardening of the gRPC step:
   - Set `ENV GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/true` so a throttled fetch fails fast and loudly instead of appearing as a credential error.
   - Wrap the clone in a retry with backoff, e.g. `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do git clone --recurse-submodules -b ${GRPC_TAG} --depth 1 --shallow-submodules https://github.com/grpc/grpc && break || { rm -rf grpc; sleep $((i*15)); }; done`.
   - Reduce the submodule surface: gRPC only needs `third_party/protobuf` (plus cares/re2/boringssl per the chosen providers) for this configuration. Clone without `--recurse-submodules` and run `git submodule update --init --depth 1 --recursive third_party/protobuf ...` for only the required paths — this drops the entire `third_party/bloaty` tree (a test/size-analysis tool) that caused the arm64 failure.
   - Better still, mirror gRPC/Abseil/protobuf into the internal registry or artifact cache the way the Ubuntu mirror was internalized in #1961, so container builds don't depend on unauthenticated github.com for ~40 clones.

**Related:** none

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `99dd5d66`

**TL;DR:** Both aarch64 "Build image" stages died because `git clone https://github.com/...` inside the container build gets `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` — GitHub is unreachable/unauthenticated from the build containers, so abseil-cpp fails to clone and UCX's `gpunetio` submodule is missing. Fix by providing credentials/mirror for third-party GitHub clones (as PR #2263 does) and by making UCX configure with `--without-gdaki` when the submodule is absent.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` #760 — the two aarch64 `Build image` stages (node IDs 233 and 205) failed; the four-way parallel matrix therefore failed while both x86 stages passed.

**Root cause:** No anonymous/authenticated access to github.com from inside the image build:

- Stage 233, Dockerfile `[2/2] STEP 32/73`:
  `RUN git clone https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp.git` →
  `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` → `subprocess exited with status 128` → `Error: building at STEP "RUN git clone https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp.git ..." : exit status 128`.
  Git received an auth challenge (or a rewritten authenticated URL) and, having no TTY and no credential helper, aborted. This is not a transient timeout — it failed in under a second, twice.

- Stage 205, `[4/5] STEP 6/6` (custom UCX build): the same failure hits the UCX submodule:
  `Cloning into '/workspace/ucx/external/gpunetio'... fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'` → `Failed to clone 'external/gpunetio' a second time, aborting` → `WARNING: Failed to update GPUNetIO submodule, continuing...`.
  `autogen.sh` swallows that as a warning, `configure` still reports `MLX5 modules: < gda >`, and the build then dies in the gdaki module:
  `make[5]: *** No rule to make target 'gpunetio/common/doca_gpunetio_verbs_def.h', needed by 'all-am'. Stop.` → `make: *** [Makefile:673: all] Error 2` → step `exit status 2`.

So one network/credential defect produces two different-looking failures; the UCX one is aggravated by GDAKI being enabled despite its submodule being absent.

**Implicated commit:** unknown — no nixl source change is implicated; the failure is in container-build network/credential setup, not in the PR's threadpool/queue code (nothing from the PR is ever compiled).

**File:** the container Dockerfile used by `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` — the abseil stage at `[2/2] STEP 32/73` (`RUN git clone https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp.git ...`) and the UCX stage at `[4/5] STEP 6/6` (`./autogen.sh && ./contrib/configure-release ...`)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Make third-party GitHub clones work in the build container — land/rebase onto PR #2263 ("ci: authenticate third-party github.com clones"), i.e. inject a token-backed credential helper or a `url.<mirror>.insteadOf` rewrite for `https://github.com/` into the build stages. Prefer an internal mirror so PR builds don't depend on external auth at all. Do not embed a token in a Dockerfile layer — pass it as a build secret mount.
2. Pin and vendor abseil instead of cloning at image-build time (`git clone --depth 1 --branch ${ABSL_TAG}` against the mirror, or install the distro/prebuilt package) so a registry/network hiccup can't break the image.
3. Harden the UCX step: stop treating the submodule clone failure as a warning, or pass `--without-gdaki` (and drop `gda` from MLX5 modules) when `external/gpunetio` is empty, so a missing optional submodule fails fast with a clear message rather than as a cryptic missing-header `make` error.
4. Re-run #760 once clones are authenticated; expect the aarch64 stages to proceed past step 32/73.

**Related:** https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2263 (ci: authenticate third-party github.com clones); PR under test: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2280

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` · commit `053752b8`

**TL;DR:** The build never failed on code — the `Allocate DL EP Environment` stage ran `salloc` on the `gb200nvl72_cx8` partition, sat queued for the full `--immediate=3600` window and aborted with `salloc: error: Unable to allocate resources: Connection timed out`. This is a cluster-capacity/allocation failure; re-run the job (or raise/reduce contention on that partition), not a code fix.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage `Allocate DL EP Environment` (node 156) failed after ~60 min because the slurm allocation for job `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep-1276` (allocation ID 2282164) was never granted on partition `gb200nvl72_cx8`.

**Root cause:** Everything up to the allocation succeeded — UCX built and installed, `meson setup`/`ninja` completed all 290 targets including the PR's new `ucx_thread_pool_engine.cpp`/`blocking_queue_test.cpp`, nixlbench built, and the test image `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep-test:1276` was pushed at 15:31:42. The pipeline then called `slurm.allocation` with `salloc -N 1 -p gb200nvl72_cx8 --immediate=3600 --time=02:00:00 --no-shell --account=blackwell` at 15:31:48. The single ~60-minute gap in the log (15:31:48 → 16:31:57) is exactly the `--immediate=3600` wait, and the terminal lines show why:
```
salloc: Pending job allocation 2282164
salloc: job 2282164 queued and waiting for resources
salloc: error: Unable to allocate resources: Connection timed out
```
So the GB200 partition had no free node within the hour and slurm returned non-zero, which propagated as `hudson.AbortException: script returned exit code 1` and `Failed in branch build_helper_dl_ep/aarch64/1`. There is no compile error, test failure, or crash anywhere in the log. Note the gap is the scheduler's own blocking wait, not a hung process — the build itself was never running at that time.

Secondary observation: because the allocation never succeeded, `jobIdFile` `/mnt/pvc/nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep/job_id_ep_1276.txt` was never written, and the cleanup stage reported `WARNING: No job ID files found in /mnt/pvc/nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep/`. That means pending job 2282164 was not explicitly cancelled by the pipeline — if slurm did not reap it on salloc exit it can linger in the queue and consume the account's priority.

**Implicated commit:** unknown — no commit is implicated; `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` (PR #2280, threadpool queue) built and linked cleanly.

**File:** Jenkinsfile / `swx-jenkins-lib` `slurm.allocation` call — see build log stage 156: `partition:gb200nvl72_cx8, immediateTimeout:3600, jobIdFile:/mnt/pvc/nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep/job_id_ep_1276.txt`

**Suggested fix:** Retrigger the build — this is a transient resource-contention failure on the `gb200nvl72_cx8` partition, unrelated to PR #2280. To reduce recurrence: (1) ask the DL cluster owners to check queue depth / drained nodes in `gb200nvl72_cx8` for the `blackwell` account around 2026-09-23 15:30–16:30 UTC and reference pending allocation 2282164; (2) make the pipeline retry the allocation and emit a distinct, non-red status ("infra: no GPU capacity") instead of a generic `exit code 1` so capacity failures are not triaged as PR regressions; (3) have `slurm.allocation` write the pending job ID to `jobIdFile` as soon as `Pending job allocation <id>` is parsed, so `slurm.stopAllForBuild` can `scancel` a job that was still queued when salloc gave up.

**Related:** none

</details>
